# Reson

> Reson is an iPhone player for YouTube videos with synchronized haptics, primarily for music. HapticLab is the internal project and IPA name, not the current product concept.

Public repository: https://github.com/tomikan1208-code/iphone-haptic-lab
Distribution: https://github.com/tomikan1208-code/iphone-haptic-lab/releases/latest
Application sources are in haptic-lab/. Workflows are at the repository root.

## User guides

- [README](README.md): Product, supported devices, installation and optional integrations.
- [Install](docs/INSTALL.md): Windows/macOS + iPhone; release assets, local signing, Developer Mode, renewal and first playback.
- [Windows](docs/INSTALL-WINDOWS.md): Sideloadly steps.
- [AI installation](docs/AI-INSTALL.md): Copyable prompts, environment facts and troubleshooting.
- [Playback](docs/MUSIC.md): Search YouTube, prepare haptics, play, adjust and use saved tracks.
- [Build](docs/BUILD.md): Fork + GitHub Actions, Xcode and release publishing.

## Design research

- [Haptic arrangement](docs/HAPTIC-ARRANGEMENT-DESIGN.md): PC neural analysis and motif composition; initial implementation completed 2026-10-07. Includes remaining research and device evaluation.
- [Real song verification](docs/verification/SERENADE.md): natori - Serenade, full-track neural/API/cache/AHAP verification on this Windows RTX 3050 PC. Native build and physical haptics unverified.
- [AHAP and layers](docs/AHAP.md): Sample layering, dynamic controls, import/export and clip playback.

## PC analysis and optional integrations

- [PC server](docs/PC-SERVER.md): Install uv, start on Windows/macOS/Linux, connect over LAN, stop.
- [HTTP API](docs/API.md): Bearer authentication, uploads, jobs, saved haptic JSON and examples.
- [OpenAPI 3.1](docs/api/openapi.json): Machine-readable contract, also served at authenticated GET /openapi.json.
- [Python client](pc-server/client.py): Dependency-free client; analyze the bundled HapticLab/Resources/MusicDemo.wav first.
- [Google OAuth](docs/GOOGLE-LOGIN.md): Optional own-playlist login; user's own iOS client ID and rebuild.

## Constraints

iOS 16+ on a physical Core Haptics-capable iPhone. No Android app. A simulator cannot reproduce physical haptics. New music arrangements require the local PC server and pretrained ML environment; cached tracks play without a PC. No LLM or cloud inference. Windows reference setup: Python 3.11, CUDA PyTorch 2.5.1, pinned Windows ports of All-In-One/Demucs, Beat This and CLAP. Initial IPA installation requires Windows/macOS and local signing. Do not ask users to share Apple passwords, verification codes, Google tokens or PC connection keys in chat. API results are haptic data, not remote control of the phone. Current source is 2.8; native build and device evaluation remain unverified.
